analysis.investment_thesis: Landmark Global is a tiny (INR 52 Cr) immigration consultancy with a near-zero 0.21% ROE — the business earns essentially nothing on its capital, making the optically cheap 5.25x P/E meaningless. Inverting: this is exactly the kind of low-quality, low-moat microcap a rational investor should never touch.
key_strengths: Asset-light services model requires little capex.
Optically low 5.25x P/E — but on near-zero earnings.
key_risks: ROE of 0.21% implies value destruction vs cost of capital.
Commoditized immigration consultancy with no moat or switching costs.
Microcap with 0% FII and 3.37% DII — illiquid and unvetted by serious investors.
red_flags: Business fully exposed to foreign visa regulation shifts (Canada/US/UK).
Tiny INR 52 Cr market cap with 72% promoter holding raises governance/disclosure concerns.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Inversion first: what would make this a terrible investment? A business earning 0.21% on equity in a commoditized services industry with no institutional owners and a dominant promoter. Landmark Global checks every one of those boxes. A ROE this low means the company is generating returns far below any reasonable cost of capital — you'd do better in a government bond with none of the equity risk. The "cheap" 5.25x P/E is a classic value trap: a fair multiple on ephemeral earnings from a business with no durable economics.

Immigration consultancy is the antithesis of what we look for — no network effects, no brand moat, no switching costs, and full exposure to regulatory changes in destination countries that can gut the business overnight. With zero FII interest, tiny DII presence, and 72%+ promoter control, this is a microcap where governance and disclosure quality cannot be verified. Pass, and keep passing.
